chunks: And Saad ibn Abdullah has narrated from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari that he said: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Armani asked Abu Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Sublime: "Allah erases and establishes what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book," so Abu Muhammad said: "Is it not that He erases that which was and establishes that which was not?" I said to myself: This is contrary to what Hisham ibn al-Hakam says: that He does not know a thing until it comes into existence. So Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) looked at me and said: "Exalted is the Almighty, the Knower of things before their existence... and the hadith is condensed."

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Allah erasing and establishing in Surah Ar-Ra'd?
ai.summary: Imam al-Askari (a.s.) interprets the verse as affirming divine foreknowledge, where 'erasing' and 'establishing' denote the transition of events from potentiality to actuality in the divine decree, rather than a change in God's knowledge itself. This directly counters Hisham ibn al-Hakam’s Mu'tazili position of *al-istihdaath* (God acquiring knowledge after non-existence), reinforcing the Shia doctrine that Allah knows all things before their creation. The brief narration underscores the theological consensus on God’s eternal omniscience amidst the unfolding of time.
